title: Add benchmark-lab adaptive batching reporting pipeline (v88)
author: Leah Chen
release_notes: Adds adaptive-batching reporting pipeline to benchmark-lab; publishes per-run batch stats, latency/throughput profiles, and profiling baselines for optimizer tuning. Includes dashboards and initial alerting.
description: Context: This PR adds an end-to-end reporting pipeline for the benchmark-lab adaptive batching workstream (v88). The pipeline collects per-run and per-batch statistics (batch size distribution, KV cache hit rates, latency p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec), materializes profiling baselines used by the adaptive batching optimizer, and writes summarized artifacts to the metrics store and S3 for downstream dashboards and regression detection. Motivation: we need reliable, reproducible baselines to tune adaptive batching and to detect regressions introduced by kernel changes or model updates. Without standardized reporting we see drift between local profiling and production behavior. What this PR does: - Introduces a new pipeline orchestration module and a lightweight runner that can be scheduled by existing benchmark-lab orchestrator. - Emits structured batch-level telemetry and rollout-aware metadata (model variant, quantization profile, hardware flavor). - Stores profiling baseline artifacts (serialized histograms, heatmaps) and wires them into the reporting UI. - Adds initial dashboards and alerts for batch-size regressions and latency regressions. - Includes a migration step to backfill baselines for the latest representative runs. Checklist: - [x] Pipeline scaffolding and runner implementation - [x] Batch-level metric collection and schema - [x] Upload to S3 and metrics ingestion hooks - [x] Dashboards (Grafana panels) and alert rules - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Documentation: README and quickstart Usage notes: The pipeline is opt-in behind a feature flag benchmark_lab.adaptive_batching.reporting.enabled. Backfill is provided as a one-off job script that iterates representative workload runs and materializes baselines. Related linear tickets: ENG-8123 (adaptive batching telemetry), ENG-8231 (reporting pipelines).

review_comments: Marco Alvarez: Please add an explicit schema version to the serialized baseline artifacts so we can evolve without breaking consumers. Also double-check the S3 path layout for multi-region reads.
Leah Chen (author): Added schema_version field to the serializer and updated backfill to write region-aware prefixes - pushed a follow-up commit.
Priya Natarajan: Integration tests look good; can we add one small e2e that runs the runner against a tiny synthetic workload to validate end-to-end ingestion?
Leah Chen (author): Added e2e job (test_reporting_e2e.py) that runs in CI with a small synthetic run; used tags to isolate flakiness.

Alexei Volkov: Observability/alert thresholds look reasonable, but we should avoid noisy alerts on training/model rollout days. Recommend a mute window and a rollout annotation on backfilled baselines - added guidance to docs.
ci_checks: ci/perf-regression: pass (no regressions against v87 baselines)
merge_notes: Squash-merged after approvals from Marco and Priya. Backfill job scheduled in production for 2026-02-28; feature flag off by default for staged rollout.
notes_for_operators: Feature flag: benchmark_lab.adaptive_batching.reporting.enabled=false by default. To enable: set helm value benchmarklab.reporting.enabled=true and supply s3.credentials via KMS. Backfill script: benchmark-lab/scripts/backfill_baselines.py --since 2026-01-01 --to 2026-02-14 --dry-run first.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: noisy alerts during model rollouts and increased storage usage for baselines. Mitigation: feature-flagged rollout, backfill window, TTL on profiling artifacts, and mute windows for deployment days.
